long_biography.plain_text:
Binder trained in architecture and also earned an MBA before building a career across environmental services and life sciences. He founded Landbell Group in the 1990s, developing a German waste-management provider into an international environmental and chemical compliance business, and continues as its chairman. Landbell expanded through producer-responsibility systems, take-back services and recycling logistics.

Binder descends from the family behind Merck and formerly held a major shareholder position in the pharmaceutical group before converting that stake to cash. He later co-founded Dinaqor and Daina, bringing his investment activity into biotechnology and personalized medicine. Dinaqor develops gene-based treatments, while Daina applies analytics to cancer care.
